messages:
amelia: incident-bot just fired a page for canary-error-rate at 20% for release/2026-03-15-canary
incident-bot: [AUTOPAGE] alert triggered: `canary-error-rate > 15%` (service: inference-canary) — page sent to oncall (pagerduty)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-4621 created and routed to on-call: `oncall-sre`. Escalation policy: realtime-pager.
sarah: acked on pd, jumping in. seeing a cluster of 500s on the canary fleet metrics dash.
raj: looking at kinesis/telemetry — there's a sudden spike in malformed tokenization events from the tokenizer microservice at ~3322107700. could be upstream.
amelia: good catch. canary traffic is 2% of production, but errors are noisy — need to know if customer-facing yet. jordan, can you confirm whether the ingress routing sent traffic to canary for a subset of prod customers?
jordan: yes, traffic split 2% by flag `rollout/2026-03-15`. No manual overrides. I see about ~1.2k requests per minute to canary nodes.
lucy: on logs: stacktrace points to `TokenStream::normalize` failing on some edge-case unicode sequences. Repro locally with failing payloads.
sarah: okay, mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout (flag rollback to 0%), 2) divert traffic from canary, 3) scale down canary nodes to reduce blast radius. Who can flip the flag?
emma: I can flip the FF. doing `./flagctl set rollout/2026-03-15 0 --env prod` now.
ops: disrupting autopilot: disabling autoscaler on canary to avoid noisy scaling during mitigation: `kubectl patch hpa canary-2026 --replicas=1`
amelia: pagerduty-bot — mark PD incident as acknowledged and add note: pausing rollout + investigating tokenizer input sanitization.
pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-4621 acknowledged by sarah. Note added: "pausing rollout, diverting traffic, scaling down canary."
raj: note — telemetry spike looks correlated with a third-party client sending batched chat messages with embedded zero-width joiners. Not all requests fail; it's a data-dependent regression in tokenizer update bundled in this release.
jordan: rollback initiated: `deployctl rollback service/tokenizer --to v1.7.12` started at 3322107900. ETA ~45s per pod, rolling.
lucy: pods restarting, logs show error counts dropping already. p95 error rate on canary went from 18% -> 4% in last 30s.
sarah: great. are any customers affected? we need to check support triage for inbound tickets and set status page if necessary.
amelia: quick customer impact check: query infra logs for 5xx rates across customer segments. @raj can you run the segment query and call out any paid customers >1% error?
raj: running query now... results: only synthetic tests and non-paying internal clients exceed threshold. no customer-facing accounts flagged.
emma: status page: no public incident needed. Will keep suppressed for now.
ops: rollback completed at 3322107970; tokenizer pods at v1.7.12; canary error rates back to baseline.
sarah: excellent. I'll close PD once we confirm stability for 10 minutes. tagging for postmortem: `oncall`, `eng-runtime`, `eng-ml`, `devex`.
jordan: follow-up action: revert tokenizer change in release branch (PR prepared: #6148) and add extra fuzz tests for unicode edge cases.
lucy: adding a short-term alert tuning: increase canary error threshold to 25% for autopage and add a secondary check requiring spike in customer-facing 5xxs to avoid telemetry noise autopages.
amelia: agree — we should avoid autopage on non-customer signals. queue a ticket for `alerting: refine canary autopage` and add me as reviewer.
pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-4621 resolved by sarah.
incident-bot: note: automated page source: `canary-error-rate` metric. root cause suspected: regression in tokenizer change included in release/2026-03-15.
sarah: closing thread here. nice coordination. we'll schedule a blameless postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT.
amelia: thanks all. action items: PR #6148, fuzz tests, alert tuning ticket, postmortem invite.
